questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I figured that when going for half a year I might as well go as far as possible and explore a corner of the world that I hadn't previously been to. I've always liked the Australian culture and been fascinated by its nature which is vastly different from anything in europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. If anything the information dump was a bit too much

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember receiving much assistance although all sorts of it was available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy to get into the private dorm accomodations, however a fair bit of money can be saved by finding a regular apartment which is my impression isn't too hard if you look on facebook in good time before arriving.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's fine to live off campus at USYD as long as you're staying within walking distance of the campus. A lot of what happens in Sydney is off campus anyways.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just registered on their homepage and applied for the units you were planning to take. If you changed your mind regarding which units you wanted, changing them was very possible, but it was a slow process as the coordinator had to manually make the changes for all the students she was responsible for. Furthermore the university was very slow to accept/decline your applications to the different units so if anything was declined you only got to know in the last minute, so it is good to have a back-up plan ready.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always e-mail the coordinator who would typically reply within 2 days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got half of the classes I initially applied for accepted by the host university. One due to them not believing I was qualified and one due to a timetable clash. If you have a timetable clash you wont be able to take both units even though the lectures aren't nescessarily mandatory.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it but have a backup plan.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academic level is quite low with a lot of time spent covering things that is covered in High school in Denmark. This was my experience in my units engineering and medical physics. In my "fun unit" (sport and learning) the contents although still fun challenged students perceptions and encouraged critical thinking. In my units in physics, medical physics and engineering the focus seemed to be learning by heart rather than critical and creative thinking skills which made them seem kinda pointless in a world with google and chatbots.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The BA course I took was challenging in a good way and contained some surprisingly advanced concepts, but it stil suffered from a "learn by heart" approach to teaching.
The MA courses involved a lot of stuff that in Denmark is assumed to be known from high school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Often attendance to lectures is mandatory which isn't the case at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHYS3036 - condensed matter and particle physics
BMET5959 - introduction to biophotonics
PHYS5012 - radiation physics and dosimetry
EDUH4058 - sport and learning in australian culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
EDUH4058 - Sport and learning in australian culture.
It is so much fun, and gives insights into many aspects of life in australia and the history of the country. The course mainly consists of field trips so you get around and see stuff all around the city and attend a lot of events and matches. It is also one of the best places to meet people although mainly international students are enrolled, but they're from all over the world.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can think of it, it was probably already a thing. They had loads and loads of clubs and initiatives

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Archery, it was fun and the club was very social.
Run clubs, getting up early and staying active is a big part of Sydney culture

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Uluru is a must see and worth every penny in spite of being a pretty expensive trip. And the glow worm caves and fruit bat colonies and other small naturall hubs near sydney.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining clubs is the easiest way to meet Aussie students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The car-centered approach to infrastructure

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The sport and active life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't go for academia, Although they're ranked higher than UCPH on international rankings, UCPH provides vastly better teaching.
Join clubs.
Get a bike to get around town. Although there aren't dedicated bike lanes like in Copenhagen, their public transport is very slow so a lot of time can be saved by biking.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Going by train is pretty cheap except from the airport where there is an extra fee, so it's often cheaper to grab an uber from the airport.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: experiencing Australias nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding time to do all the stuff I wanted to

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
